# RackMatch

> RackMatch names the IEC jumper between a server PSU inlet and a PDU outlet. It does not sell power cords.

The inlet on the installed power supply decides the cord. The chassis name alone does not.

- C14 inlet: C13 coupler into the server, C14 plug into a PDU C13 outlet. 10 A class.
- C20 inlet: C19 coupler into the server, C20 plug into a PDU C19 outlet. 16 A class.
- A C13 cord does not mate with a C20 inlet.

## Pages

- [Home](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/): matcher for one server and one PDU from the catalog
- [What power cord does my server need](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/what-power-cord-does-my-server-need/)
- [C13 vs C14](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/c13-vs-c14/)
- [C19 vs C20](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/c19-vs-c20/)
- [Server to PDU power cord](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/server-to-pdu-power-cord/)
- [Dell PowerEdge R650 + APC AP8941](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/dell-poweredge-r650-apc-ap8941/)
- [Dell PowerEdge R760 + APC AP8941](https://rackmatch.vercel.app/dell-poweredge-r760-apc-ap8941/)

Check the live nameplate. A high-watt PSU in the same chassis can use C20 instead of C14.
